explanation: Start with one way to make zero. Process one score at a time and update totals upwards, permitting repeated uses of that score. Processing scores outside the total loop counts combinations rather than ordered sequences.
timeComplexity: O(target × number of scores). Each score type updates every relevant subtotal; the actual implementation retains one row or all rows.
spaceComplexity: O(target). C#/JavaScript store target+1 counts; native versions store one such row per score type.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: After processing the first i score types, ways[t] counts exactly their unordered combinations making t. For the next score s, increasing totals add ways[t−s], allowing another copy of s while retaining combinations not using it. Score types outside the total loop prevent reordered plays from being counted separately.
walkthrough: For final score 9 and allowed plays [2,3], the two combinations are three 3s, and three 2s plus one 3. Their play order is ignored, so return 2. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: The target zero has one empty combination.
A play value may be reused.
Changing play order must not create a new combination.
